body: OK - it'll take me some time to get PHP set up on my windows machine, but I'll get on this.
I've removed that anti-Windows exception in 98454f864499f2a45cc7d7579558ba1a312de706.

I can debug anything and everything for you if you point me in the right direction. 😉 

I created a breakpoint directly at the beginning of the `Psalm\Checker\FileChecker::getStatementsForFile()` method but it is simply never called at all.


Tested with latest PHP 5.6, 7.0, and 7.1.

I've just updated Psalm to be a little more helpful – now the cache path is resolved when scanning the config.

I've added a caveat to the wiki – if you specify a cache directory, its parent must already exist.

body:
Replacing `/` with `DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR` is unnecessary in Windows. Windows has support for them since a very, very, very long time. There are only very programs which have problems with them and non of those are part of Windows.

I will investigate why psalm does not scan any files but this is definitely not a solution for anything.

Psalm does string comparison on file names to determine whether a file is in a given directory, and the slashes were throwing Psalm off. On my Windows machine this prevented Psalm from scanning itself (as you noted, no files would be scanned).

I just pushed 686891f30f6719fcfbb0d8a41707d66db8bd6fe9 which prevents an infinite loop if a config file isn't present in the expected location.

Running Psalm on Windows on https://github.com/Fleshgrinder/php-assertion gives the following output:

```
C:\git\php-assertion>php vendor\vimeo\psalm\bin\psalm -m

```

This obviously changes the game since Windows converts any `/` transparently to `\` and if you use those somewhere you'll need to normalize. 👍 

Works now nicely! 😏

This issue is definitely closed. I'm sure I'll have plenty of other stuff to complain about but not it's time to test some code. 😉
